newsitem.title: KENYA: Power firm helps Nairobi bourse index rise.
newsitem.headline: Power firm helps Nairobi bourse index rise.

text.p: Sustained activity in power distribution monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting Co helped a marginal recovery in the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index on Monday, floor dealers and brokers said.
The index gained 6.42 points to close at 3049.16. Turnover was posted at 10.698 million shillings traded on 294,134 shares from 10.584 million shillings traded on 362,901 shares on Friday.

Bourse officials said the index went up due to marginal increases in key shares and trading in big quantities on some high value shares. They saw activity centred on 24,700 shares of Kenya Power & Lighting Co at an unchanged 120, and 95,965 shares of Car and General trading at 20.

"There is a lot of buying interest in Kenya Power & Lighting Co because of its high net asset value, monopoly status and good capitalization history," a senior broker said. "It is also enjoying a lot of institutional support," he added.

There were market rumours of an impending rise in power charges after Kenya Power & Lighting Co announced that maintenance work and new breakdowns at key stations meant that shortages to the national grid would continue for some time.
"That is good for speculators. It means the power company is one area where they will make their money," a dealer said.

Kenya Commercial Bank opened 1.50 higher at 57 but slid back to 55.50 at close. Brokers said the bank now enjoyed an improved perception in its image since a recently-closed public offer, enabling it to sell its share price at a premium.
"Kenya Commercial Bank is attracting interest from buyers who were locked out during the public offer have now come to acquire them from the secondary market," another broker said.
The new issue, 11.88 million shares or 10 percent, cut the government shareholding in the bank to 60 percent. The offer closed on October 15 but allocations have not been posted.
Foreign investors bought 2,000 shares of Firestone East Africa at 24.75 and a small lot of 108 shares of Kenya Breweries at 47.
